newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish columnist on trial for insulting army.
newsitem.headline: Turkish columnist on trial for insulting army.

text.p: A Turkish newspaper columnist on trial for insulting the country's powerful armed forces said on Friday the law under which he was being tried made it impossible to make legal criticism of the army in Turkey.
Ahmet Altan faces one to six years in prison if an Istanbul court finds him guilty under Article 159 of the Turkish penal code, which outlaws insulting the army.

"I'm only a writer not a militant. Article 159 is actually aimed at banning criticism of the army, not just insulting," Altan told Reuters a day after the second hearing of a trial which began in July.
It was not known when the next hearing would take place.

The case was brought to court after the mass-circulation Yeni Yuzil daily published two articles by Altan in 1995 on Turkey's 12-year-old conflict with Kurdish guerrillas. One was headlined "Kill the Kurds".
"The Justice Ministry ordered its prosecutors to open a case against my client in the spring after military headquarters made an appeal to the ministry," Altan's lawyer Gulcin Cayligil told Reuters.
More than 21,000 people have been killed in the conflict between the army and Kurdistan Worker's Party (PKK) guerrillas, fighting for self-rule in southeast Turkey.
